key_insight: In STEMI patients, machine learning on gut microbiome data identified a distinct acute-phase microbial and predicted metabolic signature associated with primary VT/VF.
clinical_relevance: These findings suggest the gut microbiome could help refine early risk stratification for ventricular arrhythmias after STEMI, but they are exploratory and not yet ready for clinical use.
method: Stool samples from 33 STEMI patients were profiled by full-length 16S rRNA sequencing during acute and recovery phases.
An ML pipeline selected reproducible taxonomic features linked to primary VT/VF.
PICRUSt2 was used to infer pathway and enzyme differences related to microbial metabolism.
evidence_signal: A reduced-feature support vector machine achieved AUROC 0.846 with 85.7% sensitivity and 76.9% specificity in this small cohort.
watch_item: The study is limited by a very small, single-cohort sample size and requires independent validation before any practical implementation.
paper_title: Machine Learning Approach to Identify Gut Microbiota Biomarkers in Patients with ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction Presenting Primary Ventricular Tachyarrhythmias
